fields.meta_title: Workshop Registration Form With Seat Limits | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a workshop registration form that stops at the last seat, checks skill level and takes fees, with every registrant in a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Workshop Registration Form for Hands-On Sessions
fields.hero_description: Say how many seats the room has and what each one costs. Emergent builds a workshop registration form that closes at the last seat and saves each registrant to your own table.
fields.features_heading: What a Workshop Sign-Up Has to Handle
fields.features_subheading: Workshops are small and run on materials. These six parts keep the seat count and the kit order in step with the fees paid.
fields.feature_1:
Seat counts per session

Set how many benches or easels a session holds. The form shows the seats left as people register and stops taking sign-ups for that session once its last seat is gone.
fields.feature_2:
A waitlist in sign-up order

Keep collecting names after a session fills, in the order they arrive. When someone cancels, the first name on the list gets an email with 24 hours to claim the open seat.
fields.feature_3:
Skill level asked up front

Ask about experience or a finished prerequisite before confirming a seat. Answers below the level the session needs hold the registration until the instructor reviews it.
fields.feature_4:
Seat fee and kit in one payment

Take the seat fee plus any kit price at sign-up through Stripe or any processor with an API. A registration counts toward the seat total only after its payment clears.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders that say what to bring

Send a confirmation with the address and parking notes, then a reminder two days out listing what to bring, such as closed-toe shoes or a laptop with the software installed.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, in your repo

Publish the form on your studio's own domain or embed it on a page you already run. Export the full code to GitHub when a developer wants registration inside your booking app.

fields.tab_content_1:
With the safety intro done, a bench is open

Northfield Woodshop teaches dovetail joinery on 8 benches. Every registrant answers one question first: have they finished the shop safety intro? A registrant who has not is held off the bench list and offered a seat in the next 2-hour intro. The bench stays free for someone who has finished it.
fields.tab_content_2:
Kits for all 12 seats in one order by color

Tallow Street Leather runs a card wallet workshop for 12 people, and the $95 seat price covers a precut kit. Registrants pick tan, black, oxblood, or navy leather when they sign up. Five days before the session, the supplier gets one order email with the count per color, copied to the studio owner.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every fee goes back when eight don't sign up

The Fernhill Data Collective runs its data storytelling workshop only if 8 people register by the cutoff, seven days before the session. Six signed up this time. At the cutoff, the app emails all 6 that the session is canceled and refunds each $150 fee through Stripe, $900 in total.
fields.tab_content_4:
An easel every evening for series painters

Saltmarsh Studio prices its four spring watercolor evenings at $240 for the series and $70 for a single night. The room holds 12 easels. Series painters keep an easel on all four nights, and drop-in buyers see only the easels left on the evening they want.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Workshop Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Start from the room and the materials. The bench count and the kit decide most of what the form asks.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Price the seat and the kit
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Pick a minimum and a refund rule
fields.howto_step_1_des: Count the benches or easels the room holds, not the chairs. Decide what happens once the last seat goes: a waitlist in sign-up order, or a second date opened for the overflow. A count set too high means someone is turned away at the door.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down what a registrant must already know or have finished, such as a safety intro or a beginner class. Decide whether a registrant below that bar is held for the instructor to review or pointed to an easier session instead.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Settle the seat fee and whether materials are included or added on top. If registrants choose a color or a size, note it now. Each choice becomes a count the supplier needs before the session, with a lead time you should know.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Small sessions often need a minimum to cover the instructor. Pick that number and the cutoff date when you decide to run or cancel. Write the refund rule for cancellations by the studio and by registrants, since each case is handled differently.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your notes into the prompt, with the seats and fees first and the minimum last. Emergent builds the form with the registrant table and the confirmation emails behind it. Ask for changes in plain English, such as moving the cutoff one day earlier.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Sign up under a made-up name with a Stripe test card and read the confirmation on a phone. Then try the cases that break small sessions: the last open seat, a registrant without the prerequisite, a kit color nobody else picked.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Share it where students find you
fields.howto_step_7_des: Link the form from your class calendar and the posts announcing each date. A Slack note for every new registrant shows which sessions fill first, and when it makes sense to add another date for the people still asking.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is a Jotform RSVP template, a Google Form template, university and government pages linking to their own forms, and printable PDFs from a resort, a chamber of commerce and a software vendor; Semrush adds the SurveyMonkey, Jotform, 123FormBuilder, Wufoo and Formsite galleries. Every one of them is a field list. A workshop is small and hands-on, so its registration carries rules the field list never shows: a prerequisite before a bench seat, a materials kit someone has to order, a minimum headcount that decides whether the session runs, and a series sold alongside single-evening drop-ins. This page shows each rule working with the registrant table behind it and answers the template, PDF, seminar, free and Google Forms searches plainly. Breakout rooms and group invoices stay on the conference sibling; general seat caps and waitlists stay on the registration form sibling.
